question: does the imported IREE model compute the same thing as the original SmartCam model.tflite?

criteria.rule: per element: abs_err <= abs_tol OR rel_err <= rel_tol
criteria.argmax: must agree on every sample, but agreeing argmax is NOT equivalence on its own
criteria.bit_identity: not required between these two implementations, and not generalised if seen

iree.note: the vmfb E30 produced in ONE iree-compile invocation; not recompiled here

preprocessing.note: the ORIGINAL model's own config values; the model's internal MUL/SUB completes the range, so do not normalise again outside

resize.note: applied ONCE here so both paths receive identical tensors; this is NOT a claim that it matches the flight software's own resizer

layout.verified: round trip nchw.transpose(0,2,3,1) == nhwc for every sample; and transpose != reshape asserted for these shapes

criteria_value_demonstrated.detail: the worst real_example element has rel_err 1.573e-05, ABOVE the pre-fixed rel_tol of 1e-5; it passes only because its abs_err (5.364e-07) is far below abs_tol. A rel-only criterion would have failed an honest result -- the same shape of finding E25 recorded for its own pre-fixed OR rule, now reproduced on a real flight model.

negative_control.what: the IREE model fed NCHW built by RESHAPE instead of TRANSPOSE -- the layout mistake E30 recorded as P2's obligation
negative_control.why: a PASS only means something if the criteria can fail; this shows they do
negative_control.regeneration: deterministic from the stored fixture: reshape each stored/regenerated nhwc .npy to [1,3,224,224]; the inputs themselves are not stored (the test rebuilds them)
negative_control.lesson_argmax: judging by argmax alone would have accepted the wrong layout on 34 of 37 samples (92%), which is why the pre-fixed criteria (plan SS4.2) forbid argmax-only equivalence
negative_control.lesson_constant_inputs: the only samples that passed under the wrong layout are the two constant edge inputs -- a constant array is invariant under any permutation, so boundary inputs alone cannot detect a layout error. Non-constant (here: real) inputs are required.

not_claimed: accuracy: the three example images are not an evaluation dataset (no provenance of capture, no ground-truth labels, no train/test split)
flight-pipeline equivalence: the resize here is the fixture's, not the flight resizer's
AArch64, cFS or OnAIR: this experiment compares two host x86-64 paths only (those are stages 2 and 3)
generalisation to ResNet/DeepAE (stage 4) or to other compiler versions
bit identity: not required between these two implementations, and not observed
